transcript: Doctor: Hi Sarah, thanks for coming in today. How have the last four weeks been since we started the sertraline? Patient: It's been mixed honestly. The first two weeks were rough, I had a lot of nausea and my anxiety actually got worse. But the last two weeks I've started to feel a little more level. Doctor: That's a very common trajectory with SSRIs. The initial activation can be uncomfortable but it usually settles. How about your sleep? Patient: Better than before. I'm falling asleep okay now but still waking up around three or four AM and can't get back to sleep. Doctor: Early morning awakening can be part of the picture. Are you still doing the sleep hygiene changes we discussed? Patient: Mostly. I stopped the caffeine after noon and I'm keeping my phone out of the bedroom. Doctor: Good. And the mood overall, on a scale of one to ten where would you put yourself now compared to when we started? Patient: When I came in I was probably a three. Now I'd say maybe a five or five and a half. Doctor: That's meaningful improvement for four weeks in. How about the social withdrawal you mentioned last time? Patient: I went to dinner with friends last weekend which was the first time in about two months. It was hard to motivate myself but I felt better afterward. Doctor: That behavioral activation piece is really important. I'd like to keep the sertraline at fifty milligrams for another four weeks and reassess. If we're still plateaued we can consider increasing to seventy five. Are you still seeing your therapist? Patient: Every other week yes. We're working on cognitive restructuring. Doctor: Excellent. Continue that. I want to see you back in four weeks. If the nausea returns or you notice any significant mood changes before then, call the office. Patient: Will do, thank you.
